flawed_step: The assertion that local Hamiltonicity (or maximal planarity) forces a Hamiltonian cycle; triangulations with an independent set larger than its complement are non-Hamiltonian.
counterexample: Kleetope of the octahedron: take the octahedron (6 vertices, 8 triangular faces) and insert a new vertex in each face adjacent to its 3 corners. Result: 14-vertex triangulation (maximal planar). Locally Hamiltonian: a new vertex's neighbourhood is a triangle; an old vertex v with link cycle u1u2u3u4 and face-vertices f_i (in face v u_i u_{i+1}) has neighbourhood containing Hamiltonian cycle u1 f1 u2 f2 u3 f3 u4 f4 u1. Not Hamiltonian: the 8 new vertices are pairwise nonadjacent with only old neighbours, so a Hamiltonian cycle would need an old vertex between each consecutive pair of new vertices, i.e. at least 8 old vertices, but there are only 6. (Even simpler, if disconnected graphs count: two disjoint copies of K4 are locally Hamiltonian but not Hamiltonian.)
assessment_summary: The statement is false. The Kleetope of the octahedron is maximal planar and locally Hamiltonian. It has 8 pairwise nonadjacent new vertices and only 6 other vertices, so it has no Hamiltonian cycle.
